Important: the recorder writes six files: .claim.json, .inputs.json, .cmd.json, .txt, .exit, .result.json. It raises SystemExit('CAPTURE_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS') if any suffix exists. Note it checks suffixes in order: .inputs.json, .cmd.json, .txt, .exit, .result.json, .claim.json. Then creates .claim.json with 'x' mode (exclusive).

The recorder's inputs() scope: prefixes src, contracts, tests, tools, docs/parallel/lane-bridge/A-R2-20261112 — all files with suffixes {.ts,.tsx,.js,.mjs,.cjs,.json,.py,.html,.css,.sql,.sh}. Plus package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts. Plus the recorder itself relative to cwd.

So recorded_source must equal exactly that set with SHAs. Note this means the new files (tools/run-delivery.py, tests/process/*.py) will be included since tests/ and tools/ prefixes. Good.

Now I have a good picture. This is a large implementation task. Let me plan the architecture.

Key design decisions:

**tools/run-delivery.py** — thin standard-library wrapper with CLI subcommands: status, begin-write, end-write, run, request-cancel, rebind.

Required CLI trust entry: `--release <MAIN file> --expected-release-sha256 <sha>` required for all state-writing entries (and run). Plus `--owner-task` (owner task ID).

Release format (narralens.proc0-release@3):
